text:
maria: Heads-up — ran the long-prefill replay this morning and saw a kernel-routing bias that blows up gen latency.
maria: Short description: replay trace has prefill-dominant requests (avg prefill ~10k tokens, gen ~100 tokens). The kernel selector consistently prefers the "prefill-optimized" kernel path for the whole request, which is fine for the prefill phase but forces an expensive code path for the small generation phase.
aj: numbers? where's the regression showing up (throughput, p95, p99)?
maria: quick paste from the job (replay-id 2026-03-18 / env=staging):
```
trace: traces/long_prefill_batch_20260318.json
model: redwood-70b-q4f
avg_prefill: 10240 tokens
avg_gen: 128 tokens
baseline (kernel-selection off): throughput 48k tokens/s, gen p95 210ms
current (adaptive kernel routing): throughput 35k tokens/s, gen p95 380ms
delta: gen p95 ~1.8x, overall tokens/s down ~27%
kv cache hit-rate: 97.8%
```
kevin: so it's not cache misses. Sounds like switching to the prefill kernel incurs per-request overhead for the generation phase or the prefill kernel doesn't do fused gen optimizations.
olivia: could be batching heuristics too — if the batcher groups by max_seq it might pick batches dominated by prefill length and then pick kernels incompatible with fast gen.
maria: exactly. I profiled and saw most time for gen tokens spent in attention kernel X (composite path) rather than the fast streaming kernel Y that we use when sequence lengths are small.
aj: can you paste the flamegraph/snippet from the profiler?
perf-bot: flamegraph uploaded: https://perf.internal/runs/20260318/19386/fg.svg
perf-bot: top stacks (sample counts):
- attention::composite_kernel (45%)
- kv_cache::serialize (12%)
- batcher::coalesce_wait (10%)
- tokenizer::decode (6%)
maria: experiment plan to isolate root cause:
1) Replay with sequence-length bucketing turned on (preserve per-phase bucket) to avoid cross-phase batching.
2) Run synthetic generator that emits same prefill:gen ratio but with variable prefill lengths to see if selector threshold is deterministic.
3) Disable adaptive_kernel_switch flag on one canary and compare.
4) Add a tiny post-prefill kernel switch that forces fast-gen kernel for the small gen window and measure overhead.
olivia: for (2) how are you generating synthetic traces? please include exact command so infra can reproduce.
maria: synth command I used (staging, single node):
```
./bin/synth_traffic --model redwood-70b-q4f --out synthetic/long_prefill_sweep.json \
  --requests 2000 --prefill-mean 10240 --gen-mean 128 --seqlen-dist "[0.9,0.1]" --preserve-order
```
kevin: we should also try keeping batcher window small for gen-only windows. Suggest batch_max_tokens: 4096 and prefill_priority_boost: false as a test.
aj: please add a replay vs synthetic apples-to-apples run: match total tokens, same concurrency, same seqlen hist, and run 3x for median.
maria: noted. I'll run three configs:
A) baseline (adaptive kernel switch enabled)
B) adaptive switch disabled
C) adaptive switch enabled + prefill-aware routing (new flag: prefill_routing_v1)
maria: also made a small patch to the runtime to record "kernel_choice_reason" per request. It will let us see whether choices are due to max_seq, avg_seq_in_batch, or explicit prefill tag.
aj: good. timeline?
maria: start runs now, will post first numbers in ~25m. If anyone wants to piggyback, add your job to jobset 19386-kernel-bias.
kevin: heads-up: there was a perf regression on the composite kernel from last week's patch; check PR #2142 for changes to attention tiling.
olivia: when you share results, include distributions: gen token p50/p95/p99, kernel_choice counts, batch sizes, and KV-hit by phase.
perf-bot: quick summary from the canary we already ran (canary-id=cb-19386):
```
canary cb-19386
config: prefill-aware-routing: false, adaptive_switch: true
requests: 500
median tokens/s: 36k
gen p95: 372ms
kernel_choice_counts: {composite: 420, fast_stream: 80}
avg_batch_size_tokens: 15360
```
maria: that matches the regression. If composite dominates we lose fast gen perf.
aj: if prefill is the driver, maybe add a heuristic: if post-prefill remaining gen <= X and prefills > Y, force fast_stream for next N tokens. Could be implemented cheaply.
kevin: careful — forcing fast_stream may break correctness if model expects certain kv layout. Need a safe handoff. But an interim measure (canary) is fine.
olivia: can we also experiment with splitting requests into two logical phases at the serving layer: prefill RPC then gen RPC (same request id). That would allow kernel selection per-phase but touches API surface.
maria: wrote a minimal hack in runtime to split internally (no API change) and ran a 200-request smoke: gen p95 dropped to 220ms, tokens/s recovered to 46k, extra overhead ~4ms per request for split bookkeeping.
aj: promising. Let's capture regressions across models and quant levels before rolling.
maria: next actions: 1) run full sweep (A/B/C) and upload perf artifacts; 2) create a follow-up issue to prototype safe kernel handoff; 3) add a batcher test to the replay harness that preserves prefill/gen phase boundaries.
kevin: I'll take (2) and write safety checks for kv layout compatibility.
olivia: I'll own (3) and add the replay harness flags; will make sure it can import synthetic traces too.
maria: thanks. I'll post the full run results in ~40m and link job artifacts.
aj: thx, keep the thread updated. :thumbsup!
